name: TRT clinics (online telehealth)

lead: TRT clinics, increasingly online, evaluate men for low testosterone and prescribe testosterone replacement therapy. Looksmaxxers turn to them as a route to TRT, hoping for more muscle, less fat and a more masculine look.

TRT supplements or replaces the body's own androgen and is a standard treatment for hypogonadism. Reference sources note it is also prescribed for age-related decline, which they call controversial. They give little information specific to telehealth clinics, and appearance outcomes are less studied than treatment of diagnosed low testosterone.

paras: Patients typically get bloodwork, a consultation and a prescription, then follow-up labs on a regular schedule. Testosterone comes as injection, gel, patch, pellet or other forms, and users generally treat it as long-term therapy.

Wikipedia lists possible risks of TRT including higher hematocrit, worsened sleep apnea, accelerated growth of existing prostate cancer, possible clot risk and suppressed spermatogenesis, and says PSA and hematocrit should be monitored. TRT is a controlled prescription therapy, and clinic quality varies.

chain: More muscle, leaner, more masculine look
angle.text: TRT clinics prescribe testosterone so circulating levels rise, which users expect to support muscle, leanness and a more masculine look. Clinical evidence covers treating diagnosed low testosterone; appearance outcomes and telehealth providers are less studied.

lead: TRT clinics are medical practices, many operating online, that assess men for low testosterone and prescribe testosterone replacement therapy (TRT). TRT supplements or replaces androgens and can be delivered by injection, gel, patch, pellet or other forms [1].

Wikipedia describes TRT as classic treatment for male hypogonadism and notes that prescribing it for age-related changes is controversial and under study. US use rose from 0.5% of men in 2002 to 3.2% in 2013, then fell to 1.7% in 2016 [1].

paras: No studies found on online TRT clinics as a category. Wikipedia reports that a 2024 Cochrane review found little clinically meaningful short-term erectile benefit of TRT over placebo, that hypogonadal men may see modest improvements in sexual function, mood and energy, and that the TRAVERSE trial found no increased cardiovascular risk versus placebo in men with hypogonadism [1].

The FDA investigated stroke and heart attack reports in 2014 and in 2015 said safety and benefit had not been established for low testosterone due to aging, requiring label warnings. In 2025, after TRAVERSE, it removed the black box warning while continuing to monitor risks such as blood pressure increases [1]. Nevada banned TRT for UFC fighters in 2014 [1].
Reported risks include raised hematocrit, worsened sleep apnea, effects on prostate cancer and fertility suppression [1].
